nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe LDH synthesis
nodes.procedure: A uniform solution was prepared by dissolving 2.4 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.8 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 5 mmol of NH4F, and 5 mmol of CO(NH2)2 in 35 mL of deionized water. Then, the solution and a clean nickel foam (NF, 1×3 cm) were placed in a 40 mL Teflon-lined stainless-steel autoclave and reacted at 120 °C for 12 h. After natural cooling, the as-prepared NiFe LDH/NF electrode was washed with deionized water and then dried at 60 °C for 8 h.

nodes.source_text: The Fe/Ni2P/NF electrode was synthesized via a hydrothermal method followed by chemical vapor deposition. Briefly, a uniform solution was prepared by dissolving 2.4 mmol of Ni(NO3)2·6H2O, 0.8 mmol of Fe(NO3)3·9H2O, 5 mmol of NH4F, and 5 mmol of CO(NH2)2 in 35 mL of deionized water... dried at 60 °C for 8 h.

nodes.name: Phosphorization of NiFe LDH/NF
nodes.procedure: The NiFe LDH/NF electrode and 500 mg of NaH2PO2 powder were placed in separate porcelain boats, with NaH2PO2 positioned upstream in the tube furnace. After annealing at 350 °C for 2 h in an Ar atmosphere, Fe/Ni2P/NF was obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS survey confirms coexistence of Ni, Fe, P, O elements in Fe/Ni₂P. Ni 2p spectrum shows peaks at 874.5, 856.7 eV (Ni²⁺) and 852.9 eV (Ni-P); peaks shift negatively by ~0.5 eV after Fe doping. Fe 2p peaks at 725.3, 712.2 eV (Fe 2p) and 706.2 eV (Fe²⁺). P 2p peaks at 130.3, 129.4 eV (P-M) and 133.9 eV (P-O).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The survey profile (Fig. 2a) confirms the coexistence of Ni, Fe, P, and O elements in Fe/Ni₂P, aligning with the EDX mapping. The Ni 2p spectrum of Ni₂P (Fig. 2b) displays two main peaks at 874.5 and 856.7 eV... In contrast, the Ni 2p peaks of Fe/Ni₂P shift negatively by about 0.5 eV... For the Fe 2p spectrum of Fe/Ni₂P (Fig. 2c), the signals at 725.3 and 712.2 eV... In the P 2p spectrum of Fe/Ni₂P (Fig. 2d), the signals at 130.3 and 129.4 eV...
